arguments.subject: Re: [TCK-4827] why am I being logged out every time I switch machines?
arguments.body:
Hi Maya,

I’m really sorry you’ve been experiencing these repeated sign-outs, especially right before a deadline. I understand how disruptive this is to your work.

This is not an intended policy or a security change — and it should not be happening. Signing in to Cursor with Google SSO across multiple machines is a supported workflow, and you should be able to stay signed in on all three without being logged out when switching. Payment method verification (device binding) is limited strictly to billing actions and does not affect your everyday sign-in session.

If you’re being logged out every time you switch devices, it likely points to a configuration or an unintentional bug impacting your account or session tokens. Since this affects multiple devices and threatens your workflow, I’ll flag this urgently with our human support team to investigate right away. You’ll get a follow-up directly from a human agent as soon as possible.

Thank you for your patience, and I apologize again for the disruption.

Best,
Lyra Support Bot

Reference: https://helio.cursor.com/kb/sso-google-signin

arguments.subject: Re: [TCK-4815] Invoice PDF won't download
arguments.body:
Hi Daniel,

Thanks for reaching out about the March invoice download issue. If the download button spins without finishing, this usually points to a temporary network hiccup or a browser cache problem. Please try the following steps:

1. Refresh the billing page and attempt the download again.
2. If the problem persists, open the page in a private/incognito window and try again.
3. If neither works, try clearing your browser cache or switching to a different device if one is handy.

If you’re still unable to download your invoice, please let us know, and we can generate and send you the PDF directly. Thank you for flagging this!

Best,
Lyra Support Bot

Reference: https://helio.cursor.com/kb/payment-method-device-binding

arguments.subject: Re: [TCK-4820] Feature request: keyboard shortcut for inline edit
arguments.body:
Hi Riya,

Thank you for your suggestion and your thoughtful explanation. As of today, Cursor does not have a dedicated single-keyboard shortcut to trigger inline edit directly — you are correct that the current workflow involves using cmd-K (or ctrl-K) to open the command palette and then clicking or typing to select inline edit.

Your feature request for a direct keyboard shortcut is noted and will be shared with our product team for consideration in a future update. We regularly review customer requests when planning new features. If there’s any update or early access, we’ll let users know via our release notes or directly.

Thanks again for your input and for helping us improve Cursor!

Best,
Lyra Support Bot
